**PR: https://github.com/pablof7z/nostr-multi-platform/pull/2888** [...] **Bigger discovery:** a sibling worktree (`.claude/worktrees/codex+2872-wallet-builder-doc`) already had a nearly-complete, high-quality, uncommitted draft on the exact branch name I'd been told to use (`codex/2872-wallet-builder-doc`). I verified its citations were accurate (including a genuine external consumer app, `nutsack`, that I confirmed via `gh issue view 2882`) and it was more complete than my independently-written version (same conclusions, plus the `legacy_relay_hint` detail and a "validated vs. pending" status table). Rather than open a competing/duplicate PR, I adopted and finished that draft — verified every citation against source, ran the doctrine-lint smoke suite (203 passed, including the Trellis-vocabulary gate), committed, pushed, and opened the PR. I deleted my own redundant draft from my assigned worktree. [...] **What the doc (`docs/builder-guide/29-nip60-wallet.md`) covers:**
- The two things a builder does: dispatch `nmp.wallet.*` actions with a correlation id, and bind the bounded `"wallet"` projection.
- An honest "what's live today vs. pending" table — only `nmp.wallet.connect/disconnect/pay_invoice` (NWC) are actually dispatchable today via `nmp-nip47`; the Cashu/nutzap action names and the new `WalletProjection`/`WalletCapabilities`/journal types are real, tested, frozen-contract code but not yet wired to a live backend.
- Capability-gated UI (absent capability → hidden control, never a runtime failure), with the real `action_namespaces()` enforcement test cited.
- Send-nutzap and receive/redeem-nutzap walkthroughs explaining `kind:10019` resolution, fail-closed states, the operation journal, and the single publish chokepoint.
- Relay-acquisition rules, the `legacy_relay_hint` non-authoritative field, and fail-closed rules.
- No Trellis vocabulary; no secrets in any example.
- A one-line addition to `docs/nips.md` linking the new guide from the NIP-60/61 support-matrix row.
